title: Προμηθεὺς καὶ ἄνθρωποι
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 322. Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Προμηθεὺς κατὰ πρόσταξιν Διὸς ἀνθρώπους ἔπλασε καὶ θηρία.
sentences.tr: Promētheus kata prostaxin Dios anthrōpous eplase kai thēria.
sentences.l: Prometheus, at the command of Zeus, moulded men and beasts.
sentences.n: πλάσσω is the potter's word, to shape out of clay; it is the standing verb for Prometheus' making of mankind. Διός is the genitive of Ζεύς.

sentences.t: Ὁ δὲ Ζεὺς θεασάμενος πολλῷ πλείονα τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν τῶν θηρίων τινὰ διαφθείροντα ἀνθρώπους μετατυπῶσαι.
sentences.tr: Ho de Zeus theasamenos pollōi pleiona ta aloga zōia ekeleusen auton tōn thēriōn tina diaphtheironta anthrōpous metatypōsai.
sentences.l: And Zeus, having beheld the animals without reason far more numerous, ordered him, destroying some of the beasts, to remould them as men.
sentences.i: But Zeus, seeing that the brute beasts were far the more numerous, told him to break up some of the beasts and shape them over again into men.
sentences.n: πολλῷ is a dative of degree of difference with the comparative πλείονα, 'more by much'. τὰ ἄλογα ζῷα, 'the living things without reason', is the standing Greek phrase for the brutes, and it sets up the moral. διαφθείροντα is accusative, agreeing with αὐτόν and not with Zeus: the unmaking is Prometheus' to do. μετατυπόω is to strike a new stamp on something already formed, as on a coin re-minted; ἀνθρώπους after it is predicative — remoulded so as to be men.

sentences.t: Τοῦ δὲ τὸ προσταχθὲν ποιήσαντος, συνέβη ἐκ τούτου τοὺς μὴ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀνθρώπους πλασθέντας τὴν μὲν μορφὴν ἀνθρώπων ἔχειν, τὰς δὲ ψυχὰς θηριώδεις.
sentences.tr: Tou de to prostachthen poiēsantos, synebē ek toutou tous mē ex archēs anthrōpous plasthentas tēn men morphēn anthrōpōn echein, tas de psychas thēriōdeis.
sentences.l: And he having done the thing enjoined, it came about from this that those not moulded as men from the beginning have the shape of men, but their souls beast-like.
sentences.i: When he had done what was enjoined, the upshot was that those who were not shaped as men from the first have a man's form, but the souls of beasts.
sentences.n: Another genitive absolute, τοῦ … ποιήσαντος, and the subject changes back to Prometheus without a name being given. τὸ προσταχθέν is a neuter aorist passive participle used as a noun, 'the thing commanded', picking up πρόσταξιν from the first line. μέν and δέ hold the man's outside and inside apart, and ἔχειν does duty for both halves.

sentences.t: Πρὸς ἄνδρα σκαιὸν καὶ θηριώδη ὁ λόγος εὔκαιρος.
sentences.tr: Pros andra skaion kai thēriōdē ho logos eukairos.
sentences.l: Against a boorish and beast-like man the story is well-timed.
sentences.i: The story is well aimed at the coarse and brutish man.
sentences.n: The εὔκαιρος formula again, naming whom the fable is aimed at rather than stating a rule. σκαιός is literally 'left-handed', and so clumsy, and so uncouth in mind. θηριώδη repeats the last word of the story: the moral simply points back at it.
